📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A disturbing Easter Egg has been discovered in Grand Theft Auto 6, one that traps the player in a life-or-death situation inspired by franchises like Saw and Squid Game, leading to a battle with a murderer.

According to recent reports, the Grand Theft Auto series is well-known for its movie parodies and media references, some of which break the game’s realistic setting and move into sci-fi or supernatural territory. This has led players on wild-goose chases in search of UFOs, Bigfoot, and sea monsters, some of which do exist in the Grand Theft Auto universe.

Industry observers note that one thing that definitely exists in the Grand Theft Auto universe is killers, with the protagonist being the worst of the bunch. Grand Theft Auto 6 has a far more calculated murderer than most, in a sequence discovered by The Easter Egg Hunter YouTube channel, one who can trap the player in a deadly game.

Sources indicate that in Grand Theft Auto 6, it’s possible to encounter a woman with a broken arm in a cast, who is trying to move furniture into a van. If the player helps her, they get knocked out with a stun gun. This references a scene in the movie The Silence of the Lambs, where the killer Buffalo Bill captures his victims this way.

It’s possible to escape this scenario by walking away or killing the woman, but those who are trapped wake up in a storage container with a bomb on their neck. They are mocked through a speaker, similar to Jigsaw in Saw, and prompted to take part in a survival game.

It has been revealed that the player is trapped on an island, with weapons and items strewn around, and a killer on the loose. This begins a battle royale-style scenario, where the player goes one-on-one with the killer, with the hunter becoming the hunted, much like in Squid Game.

It’s possible to escape this scenario by walking away or killing the woman, but those who are trapped wake up in a storage container with a bomb on their neck.

Unfortunately for the person planning the hunt, they didn’t count on facing a Grand Theft Auto protagonist, who can brutally turn the tables and kill their captor. Winning the game gets the player their items back, along with a cash prize and a boat that’ll let them return to the mainland.

The Grand Theft Auto series loves its references, and the hunted game packs multiple in at once. While fans are still waiting for news of Grand Theft Auto 6’s online component, this game feels like something that could appear as a battle mode, though people will quickly compare it to Fortnite and similar titles.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a gargantuan game, one that took a long time to develop. As of the time of writing, the game has been out for less than a week, but fans are already uncovering all kinds of secrets, including the ability to travel back to the PS2 era via a magic portal. This is just scratching the surface, especially as most fans haven’t even finished the main storyline yet.

Sources indicate that it took years for fans to work out all the secrets in Grand Theft Auto 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, and there’s a good chance that Grand Theft Auto6 will also be teasing fans with its hidden content for a long time. This will only get worse when the online component begins, and Rockstar can keep adding content for players to puzzle over for the next decade.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Along with the Ford Taurus and the Honda Accord, this Toyota is right at the top of the list when Amer­ican families go latest-car shopping, and right at the top of the ratings in our last family-sedan comparison test (November 1995).
  • That won’t change as Toyota introduces its fourth-­generation Camry in Sep­tember, and neither will the mix of virtues that make this model a favorite.
  • See all results for used 1997 Toyota Camry for sale near 99223.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over 3,000,000 sold! Call it the McCamry. Along with the Ford Taurus and the Honda Accord, this Toyota is right at the top of the list when Amer­ican families go latest-car shopping, and right at the top of the ratings in our last family-sedan comparison test (November 1995). Since its introduction here in 1983, Toyota has diligently smoothed up, slicked up, and suaved up the Camry till the only remaining awkwardness is the unlikely spelling of its name.

That won’t change as Toyota introduces its fourth-­generation Camry in Sep­tember, and neither will the mix of virtues that make this model a favorite. We’re talking refinement of the Camry theme, not reinvention. In fact, the basic platform and powertrain carry on, though engineering improvements seem to touch every part of the car. It’s slightly bigger in each exterior dimension—0.7 inch longer, 0.4 inch wider, 2.1 inches longer in wheelbase; the same four­-cylinder and V-6 engines are modestly more powerful (up 8 hp in the four, up 6 hp in the V-6); and the interior has been upgraded to meet all the safety standards scheduled in the next few years, including the 1997 side-impact and 1999 head-­impact requirements. The aerodynamic drag coefficient has been improved to 0.30, from 0.33.

See all results for used 1997 Toyota Camry for sale near 99223.

According to recent reports, toyota is, however, tightening the Camry’s focus. It’s available only as a four-door now in three trim levels: CE, LE, and XLE. Gone is the coupe, which won over just five percent of Camry buyers. Gone, too, is the station wagon, a shape that convinced only three per­cent of Camry buyers in its losing battle against the tide of minivans. (Production of a Camry-based minivan begins next spring.).

In the past, we’ve joked that the Camry’s personality is one of aggressive bland­ness. Unlike the frisky feeling of the Accord and the athletic tautness of the Dodge Intrepid, both of which come through loud and clear before you’ve driven to the first corner, the Camry’s subtlety grows on you over time. It’s smoother, softer, quieter than the others, less com­municative, less mechanical. Instead of talking to you in the very pleasant way of those others, it’s the silent type that, you soon notice, goes expertly about its job.

Sources indicate that in this fresh Camry, Toyota sharpened the expertise without changing the per­sonality. It’s still a car that’s light to the touch: easy to steer, easy to brake. The ride is commendably free of harshness, thanks in part to mounting the suspension on isolated crossmembers front and rear. The four­-cylinder version, with its 195/70SR-14 tires, rides very smoothly and ignores almost completely the road textures that create so much droning in sporting cars. The V-6s come with 205/65HR-15s on six­-inch-wide wheels. These tires are noticeably harsher and noisier than those on the four-cylinder cars, though road nose is still quite reasonable when compared with other cars in this class. Road grip and handling predictability are well above the minimums we’d set for family cars.

See all results for used 1997 Toyota Camry for sale near 99223.

According to recent reports, the Camry V-6 has been one of the top performers in this class. The 1997 model gains six horsepower (now 194 hp at the same 5200 rpm as the previous peak), gets shorter final-drive gearing (3.93 versus 3.43), and weighs about the same as last year’s smaller car. Another performance plus: A manual transmission has returned to the V-6 lineup, available only on CE models. How­ever, our LE V-6 auto­matic was no quicker than the last LE V-6 we tested, managing 0 to 60 mph in 8.3 seconds. Expect the five-speed to trim that by about four-tenths.

On the road, the automatic’s eagerness to change down a gear or two when you press the pedal, even slightly, and the seamless smoothness of those changes give this car quick reflexes in traffic. The engine revs with the hushed moan of a Lexus. This year, traction control is optional on LE and XLE V-6 models. When it comes to powertrain pleasures, the Camry is world-class.

Still, it’s the more subtle details of pas­senger accommodation that make this Toyota a family favorite. In the previous­-generation Camry, our comparison tests show two adults fit in the back seat more comfortably than in some other brands up to 10 inches longer. We expect this Camry advantage to widen fractionally in this new model because both legroom and head­room in back are increased by a half-inch. Although the Camry is wider on the out­side, energy-absorbing padding to protect in side impacts takes up the extra space and, in certain spots, a little more. The Camry still has pockets in the front doors, unlike the Taurus, which sacrificed them for crash-protection equipment.

Those who wish to maximize rear-seat space should think twice about opting for power front seats (standard equipment on the top-of-the-line XLE). The manual­adjust buckets have excellent toeroom under them, which the power adjuster interrupts with a transverse bar. Tall folks won’t like that.

Recent findings suggest that as in most modern sedans, the Camry has fold-forward rear seatbacks split one­-third and two-thirds, allowing the cargo compartment to be extended into the pas­senger area. Here’s another think-twice: Camrys equipped with the optional child seat—it’s built into the two-thirds section of the rear seat—have that section fixed in place, ruling out all but a narrow passage into the trunk.

At the rear, the trunklid opens wider and lower than before. Space inside, however, is a bit less in the upcoming body—14.1 cubic feet versus 14.8 before. And the new car still has the conventional trunk hinges with the sickle arms that swing down into your luggage when the lid is closed.

Sources indicate that conventional is the right description for the fresh instrument panel, certainly more conventional than the old one, which tried to visually compartmentalize the cockpit by emphasizing a huge black field in front of the driver. That was the good part. The bad part was the deemphasized and totally boring padding it left for the passenger’s amusement. Now the all-new panel stretches its padding across the inte­rior in an equal-opportunity gesture that makes the interior seem brighter and wider. The glove box is 29 percent larger. The audio controls were raised to a mid­dash height, making them easy to see and reach. The climate controls have changed over to the increasingly common turn-to-adjust knobs. They’re large enough, and so obvious in their workings, that they are easy to operate in their less prominent location. The Camry continues to position its ignition switch in the dash where you can readily see it, instead of hiding it on the side of the steering column.

Recent findings suggest that toyota has proven itself to be the master of those little conveniences that add up to an exceptionally pleasing car. In this new Camry we see more clever trade-offs as the engineers cut costs, reduce weight, and usually end up serving the customer better, too. For example, the new front bumper cuts the part count nearly in half and saves weight, yet it increases protec­tion to 5 mph from 2.5. Inside, the seats recline in stepless increments now, and the buckets’ height adjusters use a single knob instead of two. Both of these changes cut costs, Toyota notes. We say they make the car better, too. Models that previously would have had retracting antennas now have the antenna screened on the rear glass, saving weight and cost. The new Bosch anti-lock brake system weighs half as much as the old one.

In a recent development, still, not every cost saver is a benefit. The LCD odometer is simply gray num­bers on a gray field, making it less visible than the glowing digits in competitors like the Chrysler Cirrus and the Dodge Stratus. And the fresh one-piece front-bumper cover now incorporates the grille into its overtly ordinary Rubbermaid-looking façade.

In a recent development, there’s been much speculation in the automotive-trade press about a possible price cut. Don’t hold your breath. Sales of the old Camry hit records earlier this year with no apparent price cutting. Were there sweeteners for the dealer? Sure, but other brands had them, too. Toyota knows all the tricks for selling cars without collapsing its price structure-tricks, we think, that mostly won’t be needed to move this shrewdly updated Camry.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A newly identified genetic eye disease can gradually interfere with night vision and the ability to see objects at the edges of the visual field. The condition may be especially difficult to recognize because people can maintain good eyesight for much of their lives before noticeable problems develop.

Industry observers note that an international research team, including scientists at the Scheie Eye Institute within the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine, traced the condition to a gene already associated with another form of vision loss. However, the two diseases affect eyesight in strikingly different ways. The previously known disorder primarily damages central vision, while the newly discovered condition affects peripheral vision and the ability to see in darkness.

In a recent development, although the condition has not yet received an official name, researchers are calling it EFEMP1-associated late-onset retinal degeneration (L-ORD). It is linked to a specific genetic variant known as p.Arg140Trp in the EFEMP1 gene. This change causes an unusually thick accumulation of material between cells in the eye.

A Genetic Discovery That Began Decades Ago.

It has been revealed that the investigation traces back to 1998, when doctors documented an unusual pattern of vision loss in a family in the United States. As researchers uncovered new genetic evidence, they were able to connect those findings to families in Europe who highlighted similar symptoms.

In a recent development, the study, published in JAMA Ophthalmology, examined three unrelated families from different countries who carried the p.Arg140Trp variant. Their symptoms were compared with those of another family carrying a different change in the same gene, called p.Arg345Trp, which is associated with the previously recognized disease affecting central vision.

The international collaboration included researchers from Penn Medicine, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Basel, Charles University, and the University of Bonn.

It has been revealed that at first, scientists suspected that the unusual symptoms in the original family might be caused by a different genetic disorder. Testing, however, failed to identify the variants responsible for that condition.

Sources indicate that "The different disease expression in this family was thought to be similar to a condition caused by C1QTNF5 gene variants. However, none of the variants associated with that disease were found," said Artur V. Cideciyan, PhD, an ophthalmology researcher and co-director of the Center for Hereditary Retinal Degenerations. "Our collaborators then discovered a upcoming variant in the EFEMP1 gene that normally causes a different disease where the macula, which is tied to central vision, is affected first.".

How the New Eye Disease Affects Night Vision.

In a recent development, the researchers found that the newly identified condition develops gradually in the outer regions of the retina. Located at the back of the eye, the retina detects incoming light and transforms it into signals that the brain uses to create visual images.

Unlike the previously known EFEMP1 disorder, which initially affects the macula and central vision, this newly identified disease begins in the peripheral retina. People may see normally for much of their lives before gradually noticing that their side vision is narrowing or that seeing in dim surroundings has become more difficult.

Problems may be particularly noticeable around dusk or at night, when the eyes must rely more heavily on specialized light-sensitive cells called rods.

Industry observers note that one reason the disease is challenging to diagnose is that these cells may initially show no visible structural damage. The gradual progression of symptoms can make the condition even harder to recognize.

However, the researchers identified a potentially valuable early clue. In affected individuals, rod cells take unusually long to recover when the eyes move from bright surroundings into darkness. This abnormal response can be detected even when the retina still appears structurally normal.

According to recent reports, "We can detect a major abnormality in the way rod photoreceptors recover in darkness with retinas that still look structurally intact," Cideciyan said. "This gives us a functional marker of disease at a stage when photoreceptor cells have not yet been lost.".

The finding suggests that changes in how the retina functions may reveal the disease before the light-sensitive cells responsible for vision begin to disappear.

What the Discovery Could Mean for Age-Related Vision Loss.

An important question remains unanswered: How many people carry this newly identified genetic variant?

Industry observers note that researchers suspect the condition is relatively uncommon, but they do not yet have enough information to determine its prevalence. Larger investigations will be necessary to establish how frequently the variant occurs and how many people may be affected.

Beyond identifying another inherited eye disorder, the findings could help scientists better understand why vision deteriorates with age. Studying rare genetic diseases can reveal biological processes that may also contribute to much more widespread retinal conditions.

"Aging is a risk factor for many medical conditions, including retinal diseases such as age-related macular degeneration, the most common retinal condition of aging," stated Tomas S. Aleman, MD, a professor of ophthalmology and the other co-director of the Center for Hereditary Retinal Degenerations. "Lessons learned from these infrequent, late-onset genetic eye diseases offer glimpses at possible mechanisms of disease for much more frequent retinal problems.".

In a recent development, by revealing how different changes in a single gene can produce distinct patterns of vision loss, the research adds to scientists' understanding of inherited retinal disease. It also highlights the potential importance of detecting changes in visual function before damage becomes apparent in the retina's structure.

The study received support from the University of Edinburgh Chancellor's Fellowship award, RS Macdonald Charitable Trust Seedcorn Award, the BrightFocus Foundation (M2024009N), the German Research Foundation (532367710), the Medical Research Council (MC_UU_00035/9, MC_UU_00007/10), the Swiss National Science Foundation (204285), the Ministry of Health of the Czech Republic (NW24-06-00083), Charles University in Prague (UNCE/24/MED/022 and SVV 2600631), and the Samuel G. Jacobson, MD, PhD, Memorial Fund.

A common blood pressure drug has a surprising effect on calorie-burning brown fat

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1184 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension.
  • It has been revealed that losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile.
  • It has been revealed that the findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension. Scientists have found that losartan can activate brown fat, a specialized type of body fat that burns energy, and improve metabolic activity in mice. The discovery suggests that an existing medication could potentially be repurposed to stimulate brown fat and support metabolic health.

It has been revealed that losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile. In a latest study published in Nature, researchers found that the drug increased brown fat activity through a biological mechanism separate from its blood pressure effects. This raises the possibility of developing treatments that activate brown fat without lowering blood pressure.

It has been revealed that the findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health. After examining data from more than 100,000 patients, researchers discovered that people with detectable brown fat had lower rates of several medical conditions, including anxiety and depression. This is the first time the research team has reported associations between brown fat and psychiatric health, adding to earlier evidence linking the tissue to better cardiovascular and metabolic health.

Sources indicate that the research was led by Paul Cohen at Rockefeller University's Laboratory of Molecular Metabolism, working with Heiko Schöder and Daniel Lafontaine from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC). It expands on research published in 2021, when Cohen's team analyzed approximately 50,000 patients and found that those with more brown fat had substantially lower odds of developing cardiometabolic conditions such as coronary artery disease and type II diabetes.

"We only looked for a few diagnostic codes in that study, mainly focusing on cardiovascular disease since that's what this tissue has historically been associated with," indicates Cohen. "The scope of this upcoming analysis is far more expansive. We doubled our number of patients and considered more than 500 codes, which allowed us to unearth many new insights.".

AI Analysis Reveals New Benefits of Brown Fat.

To investigate brown fat's relationship with human health, the researchers examined PET/CT scans from more than 100,000 patients who had undergone imaging as part of their cancer monitoring. They focused on scans showing brown adipose tissue, which can be found in six regions of the body, including the neck, armpits, and areas around organs such as the heart and kidneys.

Sources indicate that the team used an approach known as reverse translation, which begins with observations in patients and then investigates the biological processes responsible for them. Cohen's laboratory has previously used this strategy to uncover vital details about brown fat and its effects on health.

Recent findings suggest that nicolás Gómez-Banoy, the study's first author and an endocrinologist and instructor in clinical investigation in Cohen's laboratory, used a machine learning system developed by researchers at MSKCC to measure brown fat activity. The technology allowed him to assess both the total activity in each patient and the activity within each of the six anatomical regions.

The analysis highlighted that brown fat's location could be just as important as its presence. Activity in particular regions appeared to have stronger associations with certain health conditions, suggesting that brown fat may influence the body differently depending on where it is found.

Sources indicate that "For example, the axillary, or armpit, area was linked to a decreased risk of high blood pressure compared to other regions," he says. "But overall, patients with brown fat have better glycemic parameters, lipid profiles, and echocardiographic indices, as well as lower inflammatory markers.".

These findings indicate that people with brown fat tend to have healthier blood sugar levels, blood fat profiles, measures of heart function, and indicators of inflammation.

Common Blood Pressure Drug Activates Brown Fat.

As the researchers investigated medications associated with brown fat activity, they noticed an intriguing pattern. Patients taking angiotensin receptor blockers were more likely to have detectable brown fat on their scans, suggesting that these widely prescribed medications might influence the tissue.

To explore that possibility, the team conducted laboratory experiments using cultured brown fat cells. They found that losartan directly increased the cells' metabolic activity, providing evidence that the drug could stimulate brown fat rather than simply being associated with its presence.

Even more interestingly, the researchers discovered that losartan activated brown fat through molecular pathways different from those responsible for lowering blood pressure. That distinction could be especially valuable for developing future medications that target metabolism without interfering with normal blood pressure regulation.

"The fact that its different effects are mediated by different molecular pathways is advantageous, since it means we could potentially isolate them in future therapies," says Gómez-Banoy. "That way you would be able to stimulate brown fat in people with normal blood pressure.".

Additional experiments in healthy mice strengthened the findings. Animals given losartan showed increased energy expenditure, consumed more oxygen, and produced more carbon dioxide, all signs of heightened metabolic activity. Despite these changes, their body weight remained stable.

Brown Fat's Surprising Connection to Mental Health.

Beyond its metabolic effects, brown fat may have a previously unrecognized relationship with psychological well-being. The patient analysis revealed that individuals with detectable brown fat had lower rates of anxiety and depression, extending the tissue's potential health associations beyond the cardiovascular system.

"We know that metabolically healthy people tend to have lower incidence of psychiatric diseases, so it could be that having brown fat makes you more metabolically healthy, and this correlates with fewer psychiatric concerns," says Gómez-Banoy.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers also found an intriguing relationship involving selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or SSRIs, medications commonly prescribed to treat depression. These drugs appeared to suppress brown fat activity, suggesting another possible connection between psychiatric treatments and metabolic regulation.

However, the findings do not suggest that brown fat is beneficial in every respect. The analysis also identified higher rates of osteoporosis and certain skin diseases among people with brown fat, raising questions about possible trade-offs that require further investigation.

Industry observers note that the discoveries have opened several avenues for future research. Scientists hope to examine the genetics of people with particularly high brown fat activity, investigate why the tissue is associated with lower rates of anxiety and depression, and determine whether its apparent benefits can be harnessed safely.

It has been revealed that losartan may also be only one of several existing medications worth investigating. The extensive patient analysis identified additional drugs associated with brown fat activity, offering researchers a range of potential candidates for future studies.

"There were plenty of other medications associated with brown fat activity in our large cohort," Cohen notes. "This is just a start.".

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another big content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the newly introduced theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

The substantial new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

According to recent reports, these are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

Sources indicate that the Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

The other massive addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a new Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

Industry observers note that as with every major revision, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

  • We expect the 2028 CR-V Hybrid to wear a sharp latest design, with spy photos showing slim daytime running lights above a series of thin horizontal grilles, while the rear end features a light bar that stretches the full width of the SUV.
  • It has been revealed that the cabin is also expected to get a significant makeover, with the Avancier—a three-row SUV sold in Asia—providing hints about what to expect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, honda’s bestselling model—and the third-bestselling vehicle in the United States through the third quarter of 2026—is getting a complete makeover. The CR-V will follow the path set forth by the sixth-generation Toyota RAV4, going hybrid only as the CR-V enters its seventh generation for the 2028 model year.

We expect the 2028 CR-V Hybrid to wear a sharp latest design, with spy photos showing slim daytime running lights above a series of thin horizontal grilles, while the rear end features a light bar that stretches the full width of the SUV. It will likely also be the first vehicle in the U.S. to wear Honda’s new “H” logo, which was originally introduced for its future EVs but will now be applied to other vehicles in its lineup after Honda hurriedly canceled said EVs earlier this year.

It has been revealed that the cabin is also expected to get a significant makeover, with the Avancier—a three-row SUV sold in Asia—providing hints about what to expect. The Avancier skips out on most real buttons and knobs, instead putting nearly every function into a large screen mounted to the dashboard, a dramatic shift from Honda’s current setup that prioritizes physical controls. The Avancier’s interior is wrapped in white upholstery, accented by glowing ambient lighting, and features a squared-off steering wheel. Honda also appears to be switching to a column-mounted gear selector.

See all results for fresh 2028 Honda CR-V Hybrid for sale near 01519.

In a recent development, while Honda was once led by the Accord and Civic sedans, in today’s SUV-obsessed market, the CR-V has become the Japanese automaker’s most crucial model. Its biggest rival, the RAV4, was overhauled for 2026 and went hybrid only. Now, the CR-V will follow suit to stay competitive in the incredibly crowded compact SUV segment. Hybrid sales of the current-generation CR-V have been strong, accounting for over half of the SUV’s total sales so far this year, making it a perfect choice to launch Honda’s new platform and hybrid powertrain.

It has been revealed that the CR-V will arrive on a upcoming platform that Honda promises will be stiffer and lighter than before, taking a modular approach that will lead to greater parts sharing and reducing costs. This platform will presumably be adapted to underpin future versions of the Accord and Civic, along with Acura models such as the upcoming next-generation RDX Hybrid.

In a recent development, honda will ditch the standard 190-hp 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine for the 2028 CR-V, which will arrive exclusively with the firm’s new hybrid powertrain. The fifth generation of Honda’s two-motor hybrid setup will continue to use an Atkinson-cycle four-cylinder, along with a pair of electric motors, but the 2.0-liter engine will be a fresh design, featuring a new cooling system. As before, the electric motors will power the wheels most of the time, but the gas engine can also be engaged to directly drive the wheels.

See all results for new 2028 Honda CR-V Hybrid for sale near 01519.

The electric motors are more compact than before, and Honda has developed a new battery too. The company indicates the new hybrid setup will bring improved power and efficiency, targeting 10 percent better fuel economy than the outgoing hybrid powertrain. The current CR-V Hybrid makes 205 horsepower and is rated at up to 38 mpg combined. We wouldn’t be surprised to see power increase to over 220 hp—the RAV4 makes 226 hp in FWD form and 236 hp with AWD—and fuel economy nudge up to just over 40 mpg.

According to recent reports, the CR-V is expected to come with front-wheel drive standard and all-wheel drive optional, although it’s unclear if the latter will see the addition of a third electric motor. Honda will also likely include the S+ Shift feature seen on the Civic Hybrid and Prelude, which simulates a traditional transmission’s gearchanges and allows the driver to manually shift with the steering-wheel paddles.

Industry observers note that the CR-V’s chief rival will continue to be the Toyota RAV4. However, the Hyundai Tucson Hybrid and Nissan Rogue Hybrid, which both enter a newly introduced generation for 2027, will also be strong competitors. The Jeep Cherokee, Kia Sportage Hybrid, and Subaru Forester Hybrid will be in the mix too, along with nonhybrid compact SUVs like the Volkswagen Tiguan.

Recent findings suggest that the move to only offer a hybrid powertrain could see the CR-V’s entry price climb, which might alienate some buyers. Honda will also need to make sure it can match or exceed the efficiency of rivals like the RAV4 while still providing adequate performance and a spacious, usable cabin, given how closely matched the compact SUV space is these days. Moving away from physical interior controls could also upset the Honda faithful who are used to the manufacturer’s simple-to-use buttons.

Industry observers note that production is set to kick off at Honda’s factories in East Liberty, Ohio, and Greensburg, Indiana, in April 2027. Sales should begin shortly after, and with the current CR-V Hybrid starting at $37,580, we expect the next-generation model to come in at around $38,000.

For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (853 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, how often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout.
  • The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues.
  • Recent findings suggest that depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, how often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout. A large study of Norwegian college students found that those who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety one year later. The findings suggest that maintaining a consistent exercise routine could be particularly crucial for supporting mental well-being.

The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues. Their results point to the potential benefits of exercising regularly rather than focusing primarily on longer or more demanding workouts.

Why Exercise Habits Matter for Mental Health.

Recent findings suggest that depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide. The college years can be an especially challenging period as students adjust to new academic, social, and personal responsibilities. Identifying everyday behaviors that may help protect mental health is therefore an important research priority.

Sources indicate that although previous research has linked regular physical activity to better psychological well-being, many young adults remain physically inactive. Scientists have also had relatively limited evidence about how exercise habits relate to the development of mental health conditions over time, particularly when those conditions are evaluated using standardized diagnostic tools.

To investigate this relationship, Grasdalsmoen and his team followed 10,460 full-time students enrolled in higher education in Norway. Participants ranged in age from 18 to 35.

At the beginning of the study, students completed questionnaires describing their exercise habits, including how frequently they worked out, how strenuous their activities were, how long they exercised, and how many total hours they were active each week. One year later, they completed a self-administered diagnostic assessment designed to identify common mental health disorders.

Exercise Frequency May Matter More Than Intensity.

The researchers found that students who reported lower levels of physical activity were more likely to meet diagnostic criteria for anxiety or depression one year later. However, not every aspect of exercise showed the same relationship with mental health.

In a recent development, exercise frequency emerged as a particularly consistent factor. How often students exercised was more reliably associated with their later mental health than the intensity of their workouts or the amount of time they spent exercising.

Sources indicate that the researchers also identified differences between men and women. Among women, lower exercise intensity was associated with a greater likelihood of anxiety and depression. Among men, spending fewer total hours exercising each week revealed a stronger association with these conditions.

Overall, the likelihood of common mental health disorders decreased as weekly exercise increased, with this pattern continuing up to approximately 10 hours of physical activity per week.

The results also support the World Health Organization's recommendation that adults complete at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each week.

Regular Exercise Could Help Support Student Mental Health.

In a recent development, taken together, the findings suggest that exercising consistently may be especially valuable for reducing the likelihood of anxiety and depression among college students. Rather than concentrating exclusively on workout intensity or duration, maintaining a regular routine could be an key part of supporting mental health.

Recent findings suggest that however, the researchers emphasize that their observational study cannot establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship. Although students who exercised more regularly tended to have better mental health outcomes, the results do not prove that exercise itself prevented depression or anxiety.

Sources indicate that even with this limitation, promoting accessible opportunities for physical activity could be a useful part of broader efforts to improve student well-being. Such efforts may be especially relevant for students who are beginning to experience mental health difficulties or symptoms that have not yet reached the threshold for a clinical diagnosis.

In a recent development, the authors add: "Our findings show that students who engage in regular physical exercise are at lower risk of developing common mental disorders over time. These findings highlight the importance of making physical activity an accessible and natural part of student life.".

In a recent development, "Mental health among students is a growing public health concern. Our findings suggest that supporting students to be physically active may contribute to better mental health and should be recognized as an important part of a healthy learning environment.".

Funding: The SHoT study was financially supported by the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research (2017) and the Norwegian Ministry of Health and Care Services (2016). Neither funding organization participated in designing the research, collecting or analyzing data, deciding whether to publish the findings, or preparing the manuscript.

10 Fun 2026 Games That Would Make for Great Holiday Gifts

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For many cultures and countries across the globe, the holiday season is in full swing, with many households preparing to attend family gatherings, celebrate events, and, of course, starting to purchase holiday gifts for children and other loved ones.
  • Several storefronts and digital retailers have already begun issuing early Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals, with many products, especially physical video games, going on sale for 25-50% off their original sale price.
  • With 2026 being a particularly great year for newly introduced video game releases, here are 10 fun new video games that were released this year that would make for great holiday gifts for loved ones of all kinds ranging from titles intended for children to those aimed at more mature gamers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For many cultures and countries across the globe, the holiday season is in full swing, with many households preparing to attend family gatherings, celebrate events, and, of course, starting to purchase holiday gifts for children and other loved ones.

Several storefronts and digital retailers have already begun issuing early Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals, with many products, especially physical video games, going on sale for 25-50% off their original sale price.

With 2026 being a particularly great year for newly introduced video game releases, here are 10 fun new video games that were released this year that would make for great holiday gifts for loved ones of all kinds ranging from titles intended for children to those aimed at more mature gamers.

Sources indicate that mojang’s Minecraft is considered by gamers of all ages to be one of the greatest games of all time, and over the years it’s been expanded upon through numerous updates. If fans want to get an early look at the game’s first upcoming dimension in 15 years, then they’ll have to check out Minecraft Dungeons II.

It has been revealed that like its 2020 predecessor, Minecraft Dungeons II is a third-person hack and slash dungeon crawler. It follows a hero as they set out to stop illagers from threatening the world with power from the new Warden-based Sift dimension, fighting a variety of new exclusive mobs along the way.

While Minecraft Dungeons II has only been out for less than two months so far and isn’t presently on sale, it would surely make a great holiday gift for any fan of Minecraft, especially kids, as it does feature local four-player co-op allowing siblings, parents, and friends to easily play together.

Avengers: Doomsday is expected to be the biggest movie release of the decade. While Marvel fans still have to wait till late December to see the film, they can quench their thirst for action-packed Marvel content by purchasing Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls.

Set in the Japanese anime-inspired Earth-358, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is a 2D 4v4 tag team fighting game centered around the Fighting Avengers, the Unbreakable X-Men, the Amazing Guardians, the Samurai Outriders, and the Knights of Doom fighting each other to ultimately defeat the Champion of the Universe.

It has been revealed that marvel Tokon is easily the best Marvel video game released this year. Not only does it feature over 20 playable heroes and villains, but it also includes five distinct campaigns following each team attempting to defeat the Champion, with the best arguably following Doctor Doom and his cadre of iconic villains.

Industry observers note that 2026 has been great for horror titles, as fantastic games like The Sinking City 2 and Resident Evil Requiem debuted earlier this year. However, I would argue that the best horror game to gift horror fans this holiday season is Tarsier Studios’ Reanimal.

In a recent development, similar in gameplay and visual design to the Little Nightmares series, Reanimal is a co-op platforming survival horror game following a young brother and sister as they travel to their home island to find three friends. Tragically, they find it in ruins and filled with gigantic humanoid and animalistic monsters.

Some horror stories are best experienced alone, but Reanimal is one that family and friends alike will certainly enjoy playing through together as they tackle puzzles and try to solve the mystery surrounding the island and its inhabitants.

Recent findings suggest that millions of fans around the world love Star Wars. While Disney is releasing a ton of different SW products this holiday season to tantalize shoppers, people should consider gifting their Star Wars and video game fan loved ones with the surprise hit, Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

A roguelite racing game set shortly after the Battle of Jakku, Star Wars: Galactic Racer is centered around the rise of unsanctioned races via the latest Galactic Racing League, with the protagonist Shade attempting to become the new Galactic League champion.

Galactic Racer’s colorful cast of characters and intense races utilizing podracers, land speeders, speeder bikes, or skim speeders have swiftly made it become one of the most critically acclaimed SW titles in years. Fans will surely fall in love with the game for the hilarious character of Biddy Blas alone.

According to recent reports, LEGO products have become a signature gift for decades now. While many parents will undoubtedly buy their kids a few LEGO sets this holiday season, they should also consider buying them the LEGO video game, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight.

Unlike past TT LEGO titles, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight isn’t based on any particular Batman movie but is rather a conglomeration of all things Batman, utilizing a gameplay structure similar to Batman: Arkham Knight while using elements from several Batman films, comics, and shows.

Legacy may not feature as many playable characters as past TT games, but it more than makes up for it by featuring dozens of alternate costumes for each character, alternate driveable variations of the Batmobile, and a customizable Batcave on top of returning two-player co-op.

Sources indicate that some gamers enjoy first-person shooters while others enjoy simulators, but some players want more open-world, narrative-driven experiences such as those commonly found in role-playing games. Arguably the best RPG of 2026 is Rebel Wolves’ debut title, The Blood of Dawnwalker.

Made by the creators of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, The Blood of Dawnwalker is a medieval fantasy RPG set in the 14th century kingdom of Vale Sangora, following a half-man half-vampire named Coen as he sets out to save his family and his country from the clutches of the Ancient Roman vampire Brencis.

The story, characters, and world-building of Dawnwalker are absolutely incredible, but it also has a ton of replay value as players can invest in witchcraft, sword skills, or vampire abilities and even accidentally drain the blood of NPCs if they don’t maintain their vampiric thirst.

Many older gamers are more action-oriented, and while 2026 has seen many great action games come out over the past few months, like Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, I would argue that best action game to gift gamers this holiday season is Gears of War: E-Day.

The sixth mainline entry in the third-person Gears of War series and prequel to the first Gears game, Gears of War: E-Day follows COG soldiers Marcus Fenix, Dominic Santiago, Mags Carter, and Lucas Reyes as they struggle to fight a horrifying invasion from the subterranean Locust Horde on Emergence Day.

E-Day may only be available on PC and Xbox Series X|S consoles, but it's by far the best Xbox exclusive released in years thanks to its gruesome, action-packed, yet emotional co-op campaign, thrilling PvP multiplayer, and addictive PvE Horde Siege mode.

Recent findings suggest that with Legendary Pictures and Toho releasing several great Godzilla movies in recent years, many kids are growing up as huge Godzilla fans. A perfect gift to get them this holiday season is Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered.

It has been revealed that A remaster of 2002’s Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is a four-player 3D fighting game with players being able to control some of Toho's most famous kaiju in city-destroying battles. Such behemoths as Godzilla, Rodan, King Ghidorah, Mechagodzilla, and more are playable.

What makes Godzilla: DAMMR an especially great gift this holiday season is its affordable price and small file size, with the game currently being sold on PS5 for $29.99 and featuring a file size of about 5 GB, making it a quick game to download and start playing.

In a recent development, similar to LEGO, Pokemon has increasingly become a prevalent presence in households during the holiday season. While there are several Pokemon products to gift people this season, I would recommend people gift Pokemon Pokopia to fans.

Unlike the main turn-based RPG games, Pokemon Pokopia is social simulation game akin to Animal Crossing, with players embodying a human-imitating Ditto waking up in a post-apocalyptic version of the Kanto region and setting out to restore the area using its transformative powers.

What follows is an adorably charming experience as Ditto rebuilds habitats and befriends Pokemon from every generation, with people even able to create their own structures and minigames similar to Minecraft to play with friends.

One of the best games to gift anyone this holiday season is undoubtedly the 2026 masterpiece that is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for the Nintendo Switch 2.

Released to celebrate The Legend of Zelda’s 40th anniversary, 2026’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a faithful modern remake of the classic Nintendo 64 action-adventure game, with the game once again following a young Link as he set out to save the kingdom of Hyrule from the evil Ganondorf.

Being a first-party Nintendo game that’s only a few weeks old, it’s unlikely that the Ocarina of Time remake will go on sale anytime soon, but it’s well worth purchasing at full price. Especially for parents who want to introduce their kids to Link’s most famous adventure for the first time.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming revision, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in New Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

According to recent reports, the narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for New Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with latest maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two new Agents being introduced in this patch belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Recent findings suggest that sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Sources indicate that aria is the other latest arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

According to recent reports, version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this upgrade also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

It has been revealed that the big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

As always, there’s no reason not to catch up on the latest set of Zenless Zone Zero codes for some free in-game items.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A ketogenic diet may offer significant health benefits beyond weight loss, according to a new clinical trial that compared three popular approaches to eating.
  • It has been revealed that the results were especially striking for people with prediabetes.
  • It has been revealed that "We know weight loss can improve metabolic health in people who are obese," says Samuel Klein, the study's corresponding author at Washington University School of Medicine in St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A ketogenic diet may offer significant health benefits beyond weight loss, according to a new clinical trial that compared three popular approaches to eating. Researchers found that people following a very low-carbohydrate, high-fat diet experienced substantially greater reductions in liver fat than those eating Mediterranean or low-fat diets, even though all three groups lost similar amounts of weight.

It has been revealed that the results were especially striking for people with prediabetes. After just four to five months on a ketogenic (or "Keto") diet, approximately half of the participants no longer met the diagnostic criteria for the condition. The findings, published in the journal Cell Metabolism, suggest that the types of foods people eat can influence metabolic health in ways that extend beyond the number of pounds they lose.

It has been revealed that "We know weight loss can improve metabolic health in people who are obese," says Samuel Klein, the study's corresponding author at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, Missouri. "Our data suggest that if you have high liver fat content and prediabetes, reducing carbohydrate intake can have important therapeutic effects on metabolism beyond just weight loss alone.".

Comparing Keto, Mediterranean, and Low-Fat Diets.

An estimated 40% of American adults have obesity, a condition associated with increased risks of type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, and other health problems. Doctors frequently recommend dietary changes to help patients lose weight and improve their metabolic health, which refers to how effectively the body manages energy, blood sugar, and fats.

Three commonly recommended approaches are low-carbohydrate diets, low-fat diets, and Mediterranean diets. Although each can support weight loss, researchers have been uncertain whether one offers additional metabolic advantages when the amount of weight lost is roughly the same.

According to recent reports, these eating patterns differ substantially in their nutritional makeup. Low-carbohydrate approaches, including Atkins and ketogenic diets, restrict carbohydrate consumption, while low-fat diets may obtain as much as 70% of their calories from carbohydrates. The Mediterranean diet emphasizes plant foods such as vegetables, nuts, and olive oil, along with moderate amounts of fish and dairy. Ketogenic diets, meanwhile, can include considerable amounts of fat from animal products, including saturated fat.

To compare their effects, Klein and his colleagues recruited 42 adults with obesity, prediabetes, and fatty liver disease. Prediabetes occurs when blood sugar levels rise above the normal range but have not yet reached the threshold for type 2 diabetes. Fatty liver disease involves excess fat accumulating inside liver cells, which can interfere with the body's ability to regulate metabolism.

A Controlled Clinical Trial With Similar Weight Loss.

Industry observers note that participants were randomly assigned to follow one of three diets: ketogenic, Mediterranean, or a low-fat diet emphasizing plant-based foods. To ensure that participants followed their assigned eating intends, the research team supplied all their meals and arranged weekly consultations with a dietitian.

According to recent reports, the diets had sharply different proportions of carbohydrates and fat. In the ketogenic group, carbohydrates accounted for just 4% of daily calories, while fat supplied 73%. The Mediterranean group received 50% of its calories from carbohydrates and 35% from fat. The plant-forward group consumed 70% of its calories from carbohydrates and 15% from fat.

In a recent development, researchers adjusted calorie intake individually so that participants across all three groups lost approximately 10% of their starting body weight. Reaching this target took about four to five months.

By the end of the intervention, every group had experienced meaningful reductions in body fat and improvements in insulin sensitivity. Insulin is the hormone that helps move sugar from the bloodstream into cells, where it can be used for energy. Greater insulin sensitivity makes it easier for the body to maintain healthy blood sugar levels.

However, the similarities between the groups largely ended there.

Keto Diet Reduces Liver Fat by 67%.

The ketogenic diet produced the largest improvements in several notable indicators of liver function and metabolic health.

According to recent reports, participants following keto experienced an average 67% reduction in liver fat, compared with a 45% reduction in both the Mediterranean and low-fat groups. Because the groups lost comparable amounts of weight, the difference suggests that carbohydrate restriction may influence liver fat through mechanisms beyond weight loss alone.

To investigate these effects, the researchers collected blood samples repeatedly over a 24-hour period, allowing them to observe changes in hormones involved in energy metabolism.

According to recent reports, the ketogenic group showed the greatest increase in glucagon, a hormone that helps regulate the body's energy supply and promotes the reduction of fat stored in the liver. Participants on keto also experienced the largest decrease in insulin levels, another change that can help reduce liver fat accumulation.

According to recent reports, one result was particularly unexpected. Despite getting nearly three-quarters of their calories from fat, the keto participants did not show an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels during the study.

"The most surprising finding was that participants in the ketogenic diet group didn't experience an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels despite consuming the most fat," indicates Max Petersen, the study's first author at Washington University School of Medicine.

Half of Keto Participants No Longer Had Prediabetes.

According to recent reports, the benefits extended beyond liver fat. After the weight-loss intervention, approximately 50% of participants assigned to the ketogenic diet no longer met the criteria for prediabetes. By comparison, that milestone was reached by 29% of those on the Mediterranean diet and just 7% of those following the low-fat, plant-forward diet.

In a recent development, these differences are notable because prediabetes signals an elevated risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Bringing blood sugar levels below the prediabetes threshold is an vital improvement, although it does not necessarily mean the condition has been permanently reversed.

The findings also highlight a potentially key distinction in weight management: losing weight and improving metabolic health are closely connected, but they are not necessarily the same thing. The composition of a diet may affect how the body handles blood sugar, stores fat, and responds to hormones, even when weight loss is similar.

Recent findings suggest that researchers emphasize the growing importance of understanding these effects as powerful fresh obesity treatments become more widely available. GLP-1 medications, which act on hormone pathways involved in appetite and blood sugar regulation, have transformed the treatment of obesity by helping many patients achieve substantial weight loss.

"GLP-1-based medications have revolutionized the therapy of obesity. We now have a very effective pharmacotherapy for achieving significant weight loss," Petersen states. "But in addition, our study demonstrates that the specific composition of the diet can give you added benefits.".

It has been revealed that although the trial was relatively small and lasted only four to five months, its carefully controlled design offers evidence that dietary composition can play an notable role in metabolic health. Longer studies involving more participants will be needed to determine whether the benefits persist and how different diets compare over time.

The research was supported by the National Institutes of Health and the Foundation for Barnes-Jewish Hospital.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a new brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

It has been revealed that I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on rapidly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

Sources indicate that seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his strategy.

In a recent development, as for the upcoming playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

It has been revealed that fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as new minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

As you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with new special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

Beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds fresh palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

In a recent development, though it may seem like we just had a significant life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

In a recent development, seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access.

According to recent reports, starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese Upcoming Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab states you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

Recent findings suggest that you can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rob Run is a free-to-play crime sandbox where you participate in bank robberies, raids, shootouts, and risk losing everything in lobbies of up to 5,000 players. Create your own hideout, upgrade your base, and even join a clan to become the most powerful crime family ever seen. It has a familiar progression system among fans of survival games, thanks to the presence of server wipes, allowing you to write fresh stories every time.

Not only that, but Rob Run has voice chat, so all players can communicate out in the world, set up RP scenarios, and share hilarious encounters.

If you’re not playing GTA 6 or you’re waiting for the fresh era of GTA Online to begin, Rob Run is a solid alternative. However, the biggest criminals right now are the cheaters who are ruining games for everybody else.

At the time of writing, Rob Run’s Steam reviews sit at “Mixed,” with the vast majority of negative reviews pointing out the prevalence of cheaters. In response, Kefir has revealed upcoming measures in an attempt to nip the problem in the bud.

Sources indicate that the team behind Rob Run is prioritizing strengthening its defenses against cheaters, so much so that an upcoming update that’s expected to deploy new in-game mechanics has been temporarily delayed. As well as this, discussions are being had about increased security measures with the Easy Anti-Cheat team, developing their own cheat-detection tools, and expanding the in-house anti-cheat team to deal with the onslaught of hackers.

According to Kefir, they have banned over 200,000 accounts so far, but “we know that in a free-to-play game, a standard ban isn't enough — cheaters can swiftly create a upcoming account and jump right back in. To combat this, we’re exploring hardware bans. Because separate servers with stricter access requirements can be rolled out much faster, we proposal to roll those out first.”.

Industry observers note that the first planned solution is to make server access require either a minimum amount of jail time or a certain total of in-game purchases. Unlike the majority of other crime games, jail time is actually something you want to grow in Rob Run. The more wealth you have when the wipe sweeps in, the longer your prison sentence will be.

Industry observers note that players on these restricted servers will be matchmade separately from standard servers, including in Looty Bay. Depending on the minimum amount of jail time required, cheaters could be less incentivized by having to go through quite the grind before reaching regular lobbies.

The team behind Rob Run is prioritizing strengthening their defenses against cheaters, so much so that an upcoming update that’s expected to deploy new in-game mechanics has been temporarily delayed.

Of course, there’s a lot more work to be done in order to make Rob Run a zone free of cheaters. This isn’t Kefir’s first rodeo with hackers either, as their mobile game, Last Day on Earth: Survival, has also had its fair share of cheaters.

Hopefully, Kefir’s efforts pay off, but cheating remains one of the biggest problems in multiplayer gaming, especially in free-to-play titles. Counter-Strike 2 and Call of Duty: Warzone are just two such games that have been grappling with cheaters over the years. Cheat providers continue to evolve, despite developers rolling out fresh anti-cheat updates.

On November 17, Rob Run peaked at 549,661 concurrent players on Steam according to SteamDB. After such a strong start, it would be a real shame if the game is unable to reach its full potential due to cheaters holding it back. So far, the developers have kept communication open with players, which does bode well through these struggles.

The idea of descending into the depths of the unknown is already terrifying as it is, but in Sol Cesto, you're doing so because the sun has mysteriously disappeared - and all manner of unholy creatures have taken over because of it.

Sources indicate that I've always been a fan of roguelikes, so the genre alone already scores points in my book. But I suppose what makes Sol Cesto even more interesting are the visuals - in some ways, it reminds me of this Burton-esque puzzler, Jars, with its creepy-but-cute charm.

Sources indicate that now, there's absolutely nothing cute about the monsters in the dungeons here, but it's still pretty compelling to dive into the depths to take them on. The randomised elements come in grids and stages, where you can use rewards you earn to, as you might expect, strengthen your hero when you head back up to the surface after inevitably perishing.

You unlock more heroes as you go along too, with each one offering their own sets of skills depending on your play style.

Recent findings suggest that the haunting music adds to the atmosphere, so if you're looking for horror-adjacent roguelike runs before rushing into December, this might just do the trick. So, how do you play Sol Cesto? It's currently got that "early access" tag on Google Play, but I'm curious as to what else Snapbreak is cooking up behind the scenes before this is officially launched.
